serverform.agent_help: This server is reached through the agent running on it. The records file, the reload commands and the configuration check all live in the agent's own configuration, so the panel neither sends them nor asks for them here. It reads the file name from the agent on every connection test.
serverform.agent_port_help: Where the agent listens for the panel. It answers over TLS, and you approve its certificate fingerprint the first time the panel connects.
serverform.check_conf_cmd_help: Run after a change is written and before the resolver reads it. The included file cannot be checked on its own, so this names the main configuration file. A check that refuses the configuration puts the previous file back.
serverform.enabled: Enabled. A disabled server is skipped by group operations.
serverform.ensure_include_cmd_help: Runs before every change. It takes no arguments: the setup script writes both paths into it on the target, so the panel never names a file the target then writes. A main configuration that does not include the records file takes every write and answers none of the records, and this is what catches that.
serverform.group_help: Add a group first. A server in none can only be changed on its own.
serverform.ladder_help: The three commands are tried in order until the resolver is running again. The first one preserves the cache. Leave one empty to skip that step.
serverform.private_key_help: A pasted key is stored and never shown again.
serverform.private_key_placeholder: Leave this empty and the panel generates an ed25519 key.
serverform.records_help: The sudoers rules on the target are written for this path, and the panel keeps the main configuration including it. Re-run the setup script there after you change it.
serverform.rename_help: Renaming is safe. The key and the group membership follow the record, not the name.
serverform.transport_fixed: The transport cannot be changed. The secret that reaches the server is a private key on one path and a bearer token on the other, so moving a server means removing it and adding it again.
serverform.tool_paths_help: Distributions disagree about these. The setup script prints the values it found on the target.
serverkey.token_lead: Install this token on the target with the agent setup script. The panel keeps its own copy on disk and never shows this one again.
serverkey.token_once: This is the only time the token is shown. Copy it before you close this panel.
serverkey.lead_2: on the target, then run the connection test.
serverkey.rotate_question: This writes a new key pair for %s. The panel cannot reach that server until you install the new public key on it. The old key stops working at once.
serverkey.rotate_title: Regenerate the key of this server?
serverkey.rotated: The key was replaced. Install the line below on the server; the panel cannot reach it until you do.
serverkey.title: Install this key on %s

servers.restore_question: The records file of %s goes back to what it was before the last change the panel made. Anything written since is replaced.

servertest.key_changed_help: A reinstalled server looks exactly like an impostor from here. Approve the new fingerprint only after you have read it on the server itself, not over the same connection.
servertest.key_missing: This server has no approved host key yet.

setting.siem_forwarding_enabled.help: When this is off the panel writes its audit trail to the database only. The forwarding rules stay where they are.

setting.siem_protocol.help: How the panel reaches the receiver. Off keeps the trail in the database only. tls verifies the receiver against the trust store of this host.

setting.source_server_id.help: The server the drift page compares against and the one a synchronisation copies from.

setting.ssh_command_timeout.help: How long one remote command may run before it is given up on.
setting.ssh_command_timeout.label: SSH command timeout
setting.ssh_connect_timeout.help: How long the panel waits for a managed server to answer.
setting.ssh_connect_timeout.label: SSH connect timeout
setting.ssh_idle_timeout.help: How long an unused connection is kept open in the pool.
setting.ssh_idle_timeout.label: SSH idle timeout
settings.group.fleet.help: Which server the panel treats as the reference when it compares and synchronises.
settings.group.interface.help: What a browser gets before anybody picks a language or a theme.
settings.group.limits.help: Whole numbers. Each one bounds how much work the panel takes on at once.
settings.group.siem.help: The forwarding rules themselves live on the SIEM page.
settings.group.timing.help: Durations are written as a number and a unit, such as 30s, 15m or 24h.

settings.problem.unknown_kind: This setting has the unknown kind "%v".

siem.forwarding_help: While this is off the panel keeps its audit trail in the database only. The receiver stays where it is.
siem.forwarding_switch: Forward audit events to the receiver
siem.how_1a: Every audit entry leaves the panel as a CEF line on facility
siem.how_2: The dhost field carries the DNS server the action was aimed at, and dvchost carries this panel. A change across a group therefore arrives as one line per server.
siem.how_3: Every event is kept in the database first and sent from there, so a receiver that is down builds a backlog rather than losing events.
siem.no_events: Nothing to show. The viewer reads the audit trail, so it fills as soon as anything happens.
siem.receiver_help: The panel sends its audit trail here itself. Nothing is lost while a receiver is down: the events wait in the database and go out in order once it answers.
siem.test_needs_receiver: Name a receiver first. There is nowhere to send a test to.
